latest_final: The narrator murdered their spouse and tried to cover it up by making it appear the spouse had deliberately left ("You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back"), so that no one would search for the missing spouse. To do this, the narrator needed to forge the spouse's handwriting, and practiced copying that same farewell line seven times before writing the final forged letter. But the practice attempts revealed the narrator could not successfully imitate the spouse's handwriting—the seven copies all looked like the narrator's own hand rather than the spouse's, and were themselves incriminating evidence of the forgery plot. Looking at these failed attempts, the narrator sighs, "I know I'm in trouble," realizing the forgery will be exposed and the murder discovered.
